content.thrombolysis_vs_surgery: Thrombolysis was associated with a higher risk of stroke and re-intervention at 30 days. No difference was found in 5-year actuarial survival, but thrombolytic therapy was associated with a higher rate of recurrent PE requiring readmission compared with surgery (7.9% vs. 2.8%). The two treatments were not randomly allocated in the observational retrospective study; patients referred for surgery may have been selected. Analysis of the Society of Thoracic Surgery Database (214 patients submitted for surgical embolectomy for high- (n=38) or intermediate-risk (n=176) PE) revealed an in-hospital mortality rate of 12%, with worst outcome (32%) in patients experiencing pre-operative cardiac arrest.
content.ECMO_and_surgical_embolectomy: Recent experience supports combining ECMO with surgical embolectomy, particularly in patients with high-risk PE with or without the need for cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Reported in-hospital and 1-year survival rates among patients who presented with intermediate-risk PE (n=28), high-risk PE without cardiac arrest (n=18), and PE with cardiac arrest (n=9) were 93% and 91%, respectively.
content.6.4_Multidisciplinary_pulmonary_embolism: Concept of multidisciplinary rapid-response teams (PE response teams, PERTs) for management of severe (high-risk) and selected intermediate-risk PE emerged in the USA and is increasingly adopted in Europe and worldwide. PERTs bring together specialists (cardiology, pulmonology, haematology, vascular medicine, anaesthesiology/intensive care, cardiothoracic surgery, interventional radiology) to convene in real time (face-to-face or via web conference) to enhance clinical decision-making and formulate immediate treatment plans. Exact composition and operating mode vary by hospital resources and expertise.
content.6.5_Vena_cava_filters_overview: Aim of vena cava interruption is mechanical prevention of venous clots reaching pulmonary circulation. Most devices are inserted percutaneously and can be retrieved after weeks/months or left long-term. Potential indications include VTE, absolute contraindication to anticoagulation, recurrent PE despite adequate anticoagulation, and primary prophylaxis in patients with high VTE risk. Evidence for other indications (e.g., free-floating thrombi) is lacking in patients without contraindications to anticoagulation.
content.vena_cava_filters_trials_and_outcomes: Only two phase III randomized trials compared anticoagulation with or without vena cava interruption in patients with proximal DVT, with or without associated PE. In the PREPIC study, insertion of a permanent vena cava filter was associated with a significant reduction in risk of recurrent PE and a significant increase in risk of DVT, without a significant difference in risk of recurrent VTE or death.
